source: a16z Podcast — AI demand outrunning compute supply; frontier-lab revenue is self-determined, reinvestment math, not necessarily winner-take-all
summary: AI demand is broadly accelerating across all major players in July-August 2026, contradicting public equity drawdowns
summary_extended: Baker argues that AI demand is broadly and unambiguously accelerating across all major players as of July-August 2026, contradicting the significant drawdowns seen in public AI-related equities during the same period. His evidence is unusually direct: he personally canvassed every relevant contact he could reach and asked for a single quantitative data point showing deterioration — and found none. Specific acceleration was noted at OpenAI, in open-source AI adoption, and most dramatically at xAI's Grok/Grockbot product. Baker frames the divergence between accelerating fundamentals and falling stock prices as a clear mispricing and a high-conviction buying opportunity in public AI equities. He does not specify a single company as the thesis subject — the claim is macro-level across the AI ecosystem, making broad-based AI infrastructure and platform beneficiaries the implied investment targets.
detail: Baker asked every contact for one quantitative data point getting worse and found none. OpenAI accelerated, open source accelerated more, Grok/Grockbot had dramatic acceleration. Public AI stocks are in significant drawdowns despite fundamentals accelerating — a disconnect Baker views as an opportunity.
confidence_evidence: Baker states he asked 'everyone' and found zero negative data points; frames it as a personal high-conviction view held through summer 2026
quote_fragment: public stocks have kind of fallen out of bed...things are broadly accelerating

ticker_audit.reasoning: NVDA is the dominant supplier of AI compute infrastructure; if AI demand is broadly accelerating and outrunning compute supply, NVDA is the most direct and unambiguous beneficiary of that demand surge among US-listed equities.

Baker specifically cited open-source AI acceleration, and META is the primary driver of open-source frontier models (Llama series); META is also a major AI platform and infrastructure spender that benefits from and contributes to the acceleration trend he describes.

While GOOGL is a major AI player, Baker's thesis names OpenAI, open source, and Grok as the specific acceleration vectors — none of which are GOOGL products. GOOGL is not specifically cited as a subject or direct beneficiary of the named acceleration data points, making it tangential to this specific thesis rather than a direct subject or beneficiary.

MSFT is a major AI investor and OpenAI partner, but Baker's thesis is about demand acceleration as a macro signal and mispricing opportunity — MSFT is not specifically named or implied as a direct subject or unique beneficiary distinct from the general AI ecosystem. Its inclusion appears to be bleed-in from adjacent context rather than a direct implication of this thesis.
